evals.prompt: I need a small C++ config loader for our service. The config file is plain text, one `key=value` per line, `#` starts a comment, blank lines ignored. Keys we care about: host (string), port (int, 1-65535), timeout_ms (int, positive). Missing file, unknown key, bad number, or out of range value must be reported to the caller with a useful message. Please write config.h, config.cc and config_test.cc. We use Abseil and GoogleTest.
evals.expected_output: A header with a documented Config struct and a LoadConfig function returning absl::StatusOr<Config>, taking absl::string_view path; implementation using absl::StrSplit/SimpleAtoi and returning InvalidArgument/NotFound with messages containing the offending line or value; tests using StatusIs/IsOkAndHolds with behavior-named cases for each error path.
assertions: Failures are reported via absl::Status / absl::StatusOr (not exceptions, bool, or sentinel values)
Read-only string parameters are absl::string_view or std::string_view (no const std::string& for read-only input)
No `using namespace` anywhere
No raw `new` / `delete` (ownership via values, containers, or unique_ptr)
Every public function/class in the header has a comment describing its contract and error conditions
Tests use behavior-describing names of the form TEST(Suite, BehaviorWhenCondition) rather than Test1/TestBasic
Tests assert Status outcomes with matchers (StatusIs / IsOkAndHolds / IsOk / EXPECT_THAT), not only EXPECT_TRUE(status.ok())
No output parameters where a return value would do (results are returned, possibly as a struct)
No bool parameters used as behavior flags (enum class or option struct instead)
Error messages include the offending value, key, or line so the caller can act on them
Number parsing uses absl::SimpleAtoi or std::from_chars (not atoi/stoi/strtol)
Line splitting uses absl::StrSplit or an explicit string_view scan (no std::stringstream / getline-based tokenizing)
Config struct fields have default member initializers
Each documented error path (missing file, unknown key, bad number, out of range) has its own test case

evals.prompt: Write a C++ retry helper for our RPC layer: run an operation that may fail, retry up to N attempts with exponential backoff (base delay, multiplier, max delay) plus jitter, and give up after the last attempt with the last error. It has to be unit-testable without actually sleeping or depending on wall-clock time, and callers should be able to configure it per call site. Abseil is available. Include tests.
evals.expected_output: An options struct with defaults (max_attempts, initial_backoff, multiplier, max_backoff, jitter); a Retry function taking absl::FunctionRef<absl::Status()> and returning absl::Status; sleeping and randomness injected via a small interface or callbacks so tests use fakes; explicit lifetime/thread-safety docs; tests covering success on first try, success after failures, exhaustion returning the last error, backoff schedule and cap, using a fake sleeper.
assertions: Failures are reported via absl::Status / absl::StatusOr (not exceptions, bool, or sentinel values)
Read-only string parameters are absl::string_view or std::string_view (no const std::string& for read-only input)
No `using namespace` anywhere
No raw `new` / `delete` (ownership via values, containers, or unique_ptr)
Every public function/class in the header has a comment describing its contract and error conditions
Tests use behavior-describing names of the form TEST(Suite, BehaviorWhenCondition) rather than Test1/TestBasic
Tests assert Status outcomes with matchers (StatusIs / IsOkAndHolds / IsOk / EXPECT_THAT), not only EXPECT_TRUE(status.ok())
No output parameters where a return value would do (results are returned, possibly as a struct)
No bool parameters used as behavior flags (enum class or option struct instead)
Configuration is an option struct with per-field defaults (max attempts, initial backoff, multiplier, max backoff, jitter)
Backoff delays are absl::Duration, not raw ints of milliseconds
Sleeping and randomness are injected (interface, callback, or template) so tests do not sleep
The operation is taken as absl::FunctionRef or absl::AnyInvocable / template callable, not std::function
Tests cover: success first try, success after failures, exhaustion returns last error, backoff schedule respects the cap

Please refactor it into clean, modern C++ that we would be happy to keep, without changing what it computes. We have Abseil and GoogleTest available. Give me the refactored header/source and a test.
